summary: A is preferable because its tests more directly verify that the complete multipart payload survives the retry and that invalid inputs make no request. Both patches nevertheless violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add.
reasons: A verifies the multipart field name, filename, and content on the normal request using precise multipart parsing.

A's retry handler reads and compares the uploaded payload on every attempt, catching retries that resend an empty or corrupted body; B only counts requests and would pass if the retried body were wrong.
A tests both required validation cases and confirms they do not issue a request; B has no validation test.
A enables RetryAllMethods in the retry test, matching the reported POST-retry configuration. B omits it, making the test less faithful to the report even though recorded gates pass.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), contrary to the frozen contract.
The retry test supplies bytes.NewReader content rather than a wrapped/non-seekable streaming reader, so it does not fully demonstrate the streamed-content scenario.
There is no test that multipartbody.NewFile source-reader errors are propagated.
risks_b: Upload duplicates Add rather than routing through it, violating the central reuse and behavior-preservation requirement.
The retry test does not inspect multipart content on either attempt, so it cannot prove that the file body is actually replayed.
There are no tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures despite explicit coverage requirements; validation is also performed after options are evaluated unnecessarily.
